name: Serena Castellotti
summary: Postdoctoral researcher in cognitive neuroscience at the University of Florence. Her research investigates the computational and neural mechanisms underlying human perception, with a particular focus on vision. She combines psychophysics, electroencephalography (EEG), eye tracking, pupillometry, and computational approaches to study how sensory information is encoded and transformed into perceptual experience.
research: Her research focuses on the computational and neural principles governing visual perception. She investigates how sensory information is efficiently encoded and transformed into perceptual experience using behavioural, psychophysiological, and neuroimaging approaches. Additional research interests include perceptual adaptation, time perception, visuo-olfactory interactions, and neuroaesthetics.

teaching.text: Teaching information is maintained on the official University of Florence profile and course catalogue.

cv: Expertise in psychophysics, EEG, eye tracking, pupillometry, and computational modelling.
topics: Current research investigates how perceptual experience emerges from the interaction between sensory inputs, contextual information, and adaptive neural mechanisms. Particular emphasis is placed on understanding how low-level visual features are integrated and transformed into complex perceptual representations and higher-level cognitive experiences.
